proposed_widenings.name: passive_level_grant family for ClassFeatureMechanics
proposed_widenings.justification: ASI is not activated on the player's turn — it is a permanent character-progression acquisition at a specific class level. The current 'activation' family mandates activationCost, use_count resource, and resetCadence, none of which are meaningful for a one-time level-up grant. A new family (e.g. 'passive_grant' or 'level_grant') is needed that records: what is granted, at which class levels, and whether it involves a player choice.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see 'Feats') or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Paladin levels 8, 12, and 16.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_feat
proposed_widenings.justification: The ClassFeatureEffect union only contains GrantExtraActionEffect and HealHpEffect. There is no effect atom for granting a feat (or a player-choice among qualifying feats). The taxonomy v4 §9 does not list a grant_feat atom; it lists grant_proficiency and grant_spell_access but not feat grants.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see 'Feats') or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

proposed_widenings.name: choose (feat selection)
proposed_widenings.justification: The grant is a player choice among qualifying feats, not a fixed effect. The taxonomy lists 'choose' as a procedure atom but the class-feature surface has no shape that models a player-directed selection at level-up time (distinct from cast-time target selection). A choose atom or a FeatureChoiceEffect variant is needed.
proposed_widenings.evidence: or another feat of your choice for which you qualify

notes: This pattern is shared by every class's L4 (and L8/L12/L16/L19) ASI feature. The structural gap is systematic, not paladin-specific. The modify_ability_score atom is explicitly deferred as out-of-scope in TAXONOMY_atoms_graph.md §12, confirming the core effect of the ASI feat cannot be traced even if a family/grant atom existed. A 'passive_grant' family + 'grant_feat' effect atom would be the minimal widening to represent this and the dozens of similar class-level ASI/feat slots across the corpus.
